get.description:
Liveness probe — process is up. Static 200, no I/O.

ECS/k8s liveness should poll this. For dependency status (DB, Redis,
billing background tasks) use ``/health/ready``.

Deep readiness — DB ping, Redis ping, billing task supervisor.

Returns 200 with ``status="ready"`` when all non-skipped gating checks
pass, 503 with ``status="degraded"`` and the offending checks otherwise.
ECS task health checks should poll this endpoint so a replica with a
crashed meter-flush loop is taken out of the load balancer.

Redis is reported but does NOT gate readiness (R3). The replica can serve
every request without it — budget checks fail open, limiters enforce
locally, alerts still deliver off the Postgres outbox (see
docs/operations/redis-degraded-modes.md). Failing readiness on a Redis
ping would pull *every* replica out of the load balancer during a routine
ElastiCache failover, converting a documented degraded mode into a total
outage. The check stays in the payload so operators can see it.

``stripe_catalog`` does not gate readiness either: it is account-wide,
so every replica (and any rollback image) sees the same answer. See
``_NON_GATING_READINESS_CHECKS``.

The three lanes partition the submitted batch:

LeaseGrantResponse.title: LeaseGrantResponse
LeaseGrantResponse.description:
Grant and renew response — one shape, three populations.

* INELIGIBLE (``eligible=False``): the run takes the legacy per-call path;
  no lease block.
* DENY (``allowed=False``): an authoritative hard-deny verdict feeding the
  SDK's existing sticky-deny machinery; no lease block.
* GRANT: the lease block is present. ``granted_tokens`` may be 0 (an
  alert_only project past its cap) — admission then falls to the legacy
  per-call path for each call without the run becoming ineligible.

The display snapshot at the bottom is always present so the SDK can log a
last-known budget position on any of the three.

media-count provenance marker. Present only for calls that carried

MediaUsage.title: MediaUsage
MediaUsage.description:
Observable non-text billing quantities, measured inside the SDK firewall.

Billing rule: the SDK sends EVERY observable billing basis it can measure
from the request/response — WITHOUT ever reading prompt
or media content — and the SERVER's pricing-card unit (matched against the
dataset card's ``PriceVariant`` grid) selects WHICH single quantity prices
the call. A quantity is ``None`` when it is unobservable for that call —
never zero-as-default — so an unpriceable call routes to the server's
``is_unpriced`` lane instead of being billed as zero.

Why this model exists: OpenAI-compatible/Together image endpoints return
``usage: null``, so token counts are absent; for those calls these
request-derived quantities are the ONLY billing signal (verified against live
responses, 2026-07-10).

caller could backdate the proration window and have Stripe compute

pricing, budget enforcement, and circuit breaking. ``OPENAI_COMPATIBLE``

The text side is the remainder, derived server-side; documented, not validator-enforced.

OpenAI reports audio_tokens inside completion_tokens_details / output_tokens_details; Google reports the AUDIO modality bucket of candidates_token_count. The text side is the remainder, derived server-side; documented, not validator-enforced.

is_estimated.description: True when the provider returned no usage data and these counts are SDK-side length-based estimates (explicit degradation marker — the API can surface estimated costs distinctly). False for provider-reported counts. Wire shape: the SDK OMITS the key when False, so key-absent means provider-reported.

TokenDetails.title: TokenDetails
TokenDetails.description:
Normalized token usage breakdown for one LLM call.

Provider adapters populate whichever fields their API exposes; the rest
stay at 0.  The API uses this struct to compute exact costs rather than
trusting SDK-side estimates.

Normalization contract: ``input_tokens`` includes uncached input, cached
input reads, and cache-creation writes.  PricingService subtracts cached
buckets from ``input_tokens`` to derive uncached input, so provider adapters
must not send "uncached only" input totals.

Nesting contract: ``image_input_tokens`` and ``audio_input_tokens`` are
SUBSETS of ``input_tokens``; ``image_output_tokens`` and
``audio_output_tokens`` are SUBSETS of ``output_tokens`` (probed live
2026-07-10: an images.edit response reported input_tokens=222 with
image_tokens=194 in ``input_tokens_details``; the audio buckets come from
the same per-modality sub-objects — OpenAI's
``prompt_tokens_details.audio_tokens`` / ``completion_tokens_details.audio_tokens``
and Google's AUDIO ``ModalityTokenCount`` entries). These mirror the existing
``reasoning_tokens`` ⊂ ``output_tokens`` relationship — DOCUMENTED semantics,
NOT validator-enforced (reasoning is likewise unenforced). The only enforced
subset invariant is the cache-bucket one below; image and audio tokens
deliberately do not participate in it.

PricingService derives every text remainder from these subsets
(``input_tokens − image_input_tokens − audio_input_tokens`` on the uncached
slice, and the output mirror), so an adapter MUST report the inclusive
channel total. Sending an audio count beside a zeroed ``input_tokens`` /
``output_tokens`` under-bills the call; sending it on top of a text-only
total double-bills it.

uncounted_calls.title: Uncounted Calls
uncounted_calls.description: Calls SDKs admitted fail-open on the per-call path while Solwyn Cloud was unreachable, as reported on their next successful budget check. Cumulative and advisory, never priced and never in current_usage; at-least-once delivery makes it an upper bound, and it saturates at the signed 64-bit ceiling.

uncounted_tokens.title: Uncounted Tokens
uncounted_tokens.description: Tokens consumed by those uncounted calls (provider-reported where the call completed, estimated input otherwise). Same advisory, saturating, upper-bound semantics as uncounted_calls.

last_reported_at.title: Last Reported At
last_reported_at.description: When a report was last folded; null if the project never reported.

UncountedTallyResponse.description:

UnitCostAnomalyConfig.description:
Unit-cost anomaly rule (P5).

Fires when ``cost_per_request`` over the last 24h exceeds ``multiplier``
x the baseline ``cost_per_request`` computed over
``[now - lookback_days, now - 24h]``.

``lookback_days`` minimum (3) gives the baseline at least the same
sampling floor that the daily-anomaly rule and the forecast service
apply elsewhere.

``channel_ids`` references account-level ``notification_channels`` rows
(Slack / PagerDuty destinations) — same semantics as
:class:`ThresholdConfig`. An empty list means "use the project default
channel_ids" (dispatcher fallback).

card). The ``code`` is deliberately the SAME word ingest uses for the same
